title: Made a Greek-mythology deckbuilding roguelike (Slay the Spire-style)..  looking for early playtesters
author: Putrid-Permission421
selftext:
I've been solo-building **Pantheon: Trials of Olympus**, a card-based dungeon crawler where you draft a deck and fight your way up through the Greek pantheon — mortal monsters, Titans, and eventually the gods themselves as bosses. So far, my only play testers have been my sons (14 and 8 years old). Primarily Claude Code > Fly. 

It's free to play in-browser, no download needed. Runs on desktop and mobile.

**Play here:** [https://pantheon-tcg.fly.dev](https://pantheon-tcg.fly.dev/)  
**Passphrase:** `olympus-open`

Still in early beta, so a few things to expect:

* This is early — expect rough edges, and there's a bug-report button (caterpillar icon) on every screen if something breaks or feels off
* Screenshot capture on bug reports can fail during combat — if that happens, just describe what happened in the text box
* Would love feedback on: card balance, difficulty curve, and whether the "climb a god's path" structure is clear
* Simply playing the game helps me collect telemetry, but submitting bug/feedback is even better

Thanks in advance to anyone who gives it a shot — genuinely appreciate the time.

comments.author: Lambda7Tech
comments.body:
for first game, i don't think you should have players drafting 15 cards they have no idea about, better to give a premade deck to get started and into the tutorial.  
there's not much thinking involved after spending up all my cards cause I happend to have the card that reduces faith and that made every 1 cost card 0, so I burned through all of them from my hand, then every turn there was nothing to do but just click the 1 card that was drawn every turn  
slay the spire makes player think more because each turn is a new hand that requires hard choices so i recommend doing something like that instead of single card draw or to keep single card draw you would need to give player a full hand once they empty out

replies.author: Putrid-Permission421
replies.body:
Thanks for this! Genuinely useful, and you called out a real bug, not just a preference thing. Here's what I did with it:

**The empty-hand dead zone:** you're right, and I found the actual cause. One of the early cards (Fleet Herald) discounted *every* card in your hand by 1 Faith for the turn. Combined with how the hand economy works (no full redraw, you draw exactly 1 card a turn, unplayed cards carry over), that let you zero out a whole hand of cheap cards in one turn and then be stuck with nothing but a single draw for several turns after, which is exactly what you hit. I capped that effect to the 3 costliest cards in hand instead of all of them, so the "dump a combo turn" payoff is still real but it can't hollow out your whole hand anymore.

On the broader ask (full-hand redraw like StS), I hear you, but that's a deliberate design choice, not an oversight: we want unplayed cards to persist and matter turn to turn rather than resetting every hand. What I did add is a one-time tip that fires the first time your hand actually hits empty, explaining that it's expected and you'll draw again next turn, so at least it won't read as the game running out of content the way it did for you.

**Muster draft:** also fair. New players draft 15 cards from a pool they've never seen, with zero signal. I added a "SUGGESTED" highlight on one of the 3 choices each round for first-time accounts (based on raw combat value per Faith cost), fully optional, every card's still tappable, but if you don't know what anything does yet you can just follow the highlight and get a coherent starting deck. I didn't rip out the draft itself since it's tied into the game's actual story beat (mustering your band), but this should close the "I have no idea what I'm picking" gap.

**Young Oracle:** confirmed. It cost 1 Faith to draw 1 card, which is just a wash. Dropped its cost to 0, so it's now a genuine free "swap a dead card for a random one" cantrip instead of a card with no reason to ever be played.

All of this is live now. Appreciate you taking the time to write it up in detail, this is exactly the kind of feedback that's actually actionable.
